paragraphs.source_en: This sort of big-picture thinking is central to the statistical basis of entropic reasoning. Just as any lottery ticket has the same chance of win ning as any other, after many tosses of War and Peace any particular order ing of the pages is just as likely to occur as any other. What makes the statistical reasoning fly is our declaration that there are two interesting classes of page configurations: ordered and disordered. The first class has one member (the correct page ordering 1, 2; 3, 4; and so on) while the second class has a huge number of members (every other possible page ordering). These two classes are a sensible set to use since, as above, they capture the overall, gross assessment you'd make on thumbing through any given page arrangement.

However, the number of possible page arrangements in each of these new subclasses is still extremely small compared with the number in the fully disordered class.
